# Feature parity

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:parity` from each adapter's declaration.ts under src/adapters and the feature registry (a file per group under src/features/host, src/features/connector and src/features/terminal): edit those, not this page. -->

What each tool teamrig runs on supports, feature by feature, as its adapter declares it. After a declaration or the registry changes, `npm run check` fails until `npm run docs:parity` redraws this page.

A cell reads:

- **supported**: the feature runs on this tool. `proved on` names the operating systems with a live proof, the record of a run on a real install of the tool. A row counts as proved on an operating system only with a proof made there, so `unproved` says no such record exists yet, not that the feature fails.
- **partial**: part of it runs. The cell says what is missing, then where the rest is proved.
- **unsupported**: it does not run on this tool. The cell says why.

## Connectors

The outside tools holding a team's issues (the `tracker` rows) or its code and pull requests (the `codehost` rows).

- GitHub (`github`), built on plugin API 0.1.0
- Jira (`jira`), built on plugin API 0.1.0
- Local (`local`), built on plugin API 0.1.0

### tracker

| Feature | What it does | GitHub | Jira | Local |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tracker.issue-import` | a task per open issue, kept in step with it (`issue sync`) | supported, unproved | partial (missing: a description's formatting, and the reporter's tie to the project), unproved | unsupported: the local connector keeps tasks in the register: it has no outside tracker or code host |
| `tracker.accept-label` | an outsider's issue is taken once one of the team's people labels it accepted | supported, unproved | unsupported: the Jira connector does not read who put a label on an issue yet, so the accept label takes no issue | unsupported: the local connector keeps tasks in the register: it has no outside tracker or code host |
| `tracker.watch` | a look for changes every few seconds, a sync only after one (`issue watch`) | supported, unproved | partial (missing: a free look for a change), unproved | unsupported: the local connector keeps tasks in the register: it has no outside tracker or code host |
| `tracker.issue-open` | opening a task's issue with its labels (`add --issue`, `issue migrate`) | supported, unproved | partial (missing: Markdown, and a type chosen for one issue), unproved | unsupported: the local connector keeps tasks in the register: it has no outside tracker or code host |
| `tracker.comment` | a comment on an issue (`issue reply`) | supported, unproved | partial (missing: Markdown), unproved | unsupported: the local connector keeps tasks in the register: it has no outside tracker or code host |
| `tracker.edit-body` | rewriting an issue's body (`issue edit-body`) | supported, unproved | partial (missing: Markdown), unproved | unsupported: the local connector keeps tasks in the register: it has no outside tracker or code host |
| `tracker.close` | closing an issue as completed, not planned or duplicate (`issue close`) | supported, unproved | partial (missing: a link from a duplicate to its original, and a reason the project's workflow has no name for), unproved | unsupported: the local connector keeps tasks in the register: it has no outside tracker or code host |
| `tracker.labels` | adding, removing and making labels (`issue label`) | supported, unproved | partial (missing: a label made with a colour and a description, and a name holding a space), unproved | unsupported: the local connector keeps tasks in the register: it has no outside tracker or code host |
| `tracker.status-push` | a status label per active task, its owner as assignee (`issue push`) | supported, unproved | partial (missing: a second assignee), unproved | unsupported: the local connector keeps tasks in the register: it has no outside tracker or code host |
| `tracker.assign` | assigning and unassigning people (`issue assign`) | supported, unproved | partial (missing: a second assignee), unproved | unsupported: the local connector keeps tasks in the register: it has no outside tracker or code host |
| `tracker.claims` | a commenter's take line assigns them, and an idle claim is taken off | supported, unproved | unsupported: a claim line takes only an issue that carries the accept label, and the Jira connector does not read who put a label on an issue yet | unsupported: the local connector keeps tasks in the register: it has no outside tracker or code host |
| `tracker.clocks` | the response clock: threads waiting on an answer from the team | supported, unproved | partial (missing: a commenter's tie to the project), unproved | unsupported: the local connector keeps tasks in the register: it has no outside tracker or code host |
| `tracker.mentions` | a post naming one of the team's people wakes their session | supported, unproved | unsupported: the Jira connector does not read comments for a mention yet | unsupported: the local connector keeps tasks in the register: it has no outside tracker or code host |
| `tracker.follow` | a session hears the changes on an item it follows (`follow`) | supported, unproved | supported, unproved | unsupported: the local connector keeps tasks in the register: it has no outside tracker or code host |
| `tracker.links` | parent and blocker links between issues (`issue links`) | supported, unproved | unsupported: the Jira connector does not read or write issue links yet | unsupported: the local connector keeps tasks in the register: it has no outside tracker or code host |
| `tracker.fields` | a task's priority and type written to issue fields | supported, unproved | unsupported: the Jira connector does not write an issue's priority or type yet | unsupported: the local connector keeps tasks in the register: it has no outside tracker or code host |
| `tracker.similar` | finding imported issues alike (`issue similar`) | supported, unproved | supported, unproved | unsupported: the local connector keeps tasks in the register: it has no outside tracker or code host |
| `tracker.security-alert` | a security-labelled issue pages the lead | supported, unproved | supported, unproved | unsupported: the local connector keeps tasks in the register: it has no outside tracker or code host |
| `tracker.stamp` | posted text ends with the made-with-teamrig footer | supported, unproved | supported, unproved | unsupported: the local connector keeps tasks in the register: it has no outside tracker or code host |
| `tracker.hidden-mark` | a mark on an issue that its readers do not see | unsupported: GitHub shows every mark on an issue to its readers: a mark there is a label or a comment | unsupported: the Jira connector keeps no hidden mark on an issue yet | unsupported: the local connector keeps tasks in the register: it has no outside tracker or code host |

| `codehost.pr-conflicts` | the files a pull request conflicts on (`pr conflicts`) | supported, unproved | unsupported: Jira is a tracker: pull requests, their checks and their reviews need a code host connector | unsupported: the local connector keeps tasks in the register: it has no outside tracker or code host |
| `codehost.review-posts` | review comments and reviews in the mention scan | supported, unproved | unsupported: Jira is a tracker: pull requests, their checks and their reviews need a code host connector | unsupported: the local connector keeps tasks in the register: it has no outside tracker or code host |
| `codehost.linked-pulls` | how many open pull requests close an issue | supported, unproved | unsupported: Jira is a tracker: pull requests, their checks and their reviews need a code host connector | unsupported: the local connector keeps tasks in the register: it has no outside tracker or code host |

## Terminals

The programs whose panes the sessions run in.

- tmux (`tmux`), built on plugin API 0.1.0
- Windows Terminal (`windows-terminal`), built on plugin API 0.1.0
- macOS Terminal (`macos-terminal`), built on plugin API 0.1.0
- GNOME Terminal (`gnome-terminal`), built on plugin API 0.1.0
- Konsole (`konsole`), built on plugin API 0.1.0
- x-terminal-emulator (`x-terminal-emulator`), built on plugin API 0.1.0

### pane

| Feature | What it does | tmux | Windows Terminal | macOS Terminal | GNOME Terminal | Konsole | x-terminal-emulator |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pane.open` | opens a pane for a session and answers its own id of it | supported, unproved | supported, unproved | partial (missing: an id of the pane it opened), unproved | partial (missing: an id of the pane it opened), unproved | partial (missing: an id of the pane it opened), unproved | supported, unproved |
| `pane.window` | opens a pane in the window teamrig names, made when none of that name is open | unsupported: a pane opens in the tmux session teamrig runs in: teamrig names no other | supported, unproved | unsupported: every pane is a window of its own | unsupported: a pane opens in the window GNOME Terminal picks: teamrig names none | unsupported: a pane opens in the window Konsole picks: teamrig names none | unsupported: every pane is a window of its own |
| `pane.focus` | brings a session's pane forward | supported, unproved | supported, unproved | unsupported: teamrig does not ask Terminal for it yet | unsupported: GNOME Terminal has no call for it on a tab already open | unsupported: teamrig does not ask Konsole for it yet | unsupported: the terminal has no call for it on a window already open |
| `pane.close` | closes a session's pane | unsupported: teamrig does not ask tmux for it yet | unsupported: Windows Terminal has no call for it on a tab already open | unsupported: teamrig does not ask Terminal for it yet | unsupported: GNOME Terminal has no call for it on a tab already open | unsupported: teamrig does not ask Konsole for it yet | unsupported: the terminal has no call for it on a window already open |
| `pane.restart` | restarts a pane's command, resuming the conversation when asked | unsupported: teamrig does not ask tmux for it yet | unsupported: Windows Terminal has no call for it on a tab already open | unsupported: teamrig does not ask Terminal for it yet | unsupported: GNOME Terminal has no call for it on a tab already open | unsupported: teamrig does not ask Konsole for it yet | unsupported: the terminal has no call for it on a window already open |
| `pane.rename` | changes a pane's title | unsupported: teamrig does not ask tmux for it yet | unsupported: Windows Terminal has no call for it on a tab already open | unsupported: teamrig does not ask Terminal for it yet | unsupported: GNOME Terminal has no call for it on a tab already open | unsupported: teamrig does not ask Konsole for it yet | unsupported: the terminal has no call for it on a window already open |
| `pane.deliver` | delivers a wake only to an idle pane, with its token; else says what held it | unsupported: tmux cannot tell whether a pane is idle | unsupported: Windows Terminal cannot tell whether a pane is idle | unsupported: Terminal cannot tell whether a pane is idle | unsupported: GNOME Terminal cannot tell whether a pane is idle | unsupported: Konsole cannot tell whether a pane is idle | unsupported: the terminal cannot tell whether a pane is idle |
| `pane.is-idle` | says whether a pane is idle, busy, asking, holding a draft or gone | unsupported: tmux cannot tell whether a pane is idle | unsupported: Windows Terminal cannot tell whether a pane is idle | unsupported: Terminal cannot tell whether a pane is idle | unsupported: GNOME Terminal cannot tell whether a pane is idle | unsupported: Konsole cannot tell whether a pane is idle | unsupported: the terminal cannot tell whether a pane is idle |
| `pane.list` | lists every pane it has, each with its state and its identity label | unsupported: teamrig does not ask tmux for it yet | unsupported: teamrig does not ask Windows Terminal for its tabs yet | unsupported: teamrig does not ask Terminal for it yet | unsupported: GNOME Terminal has no call for it on a tab already open | unsupported: teamrig does not ask Konsole for it yet | unsupported: the terminal has no call for it on a window already open |
| `pane.sees-draft` | sees a pane's unsent input, so a wake never lands on a person's text | unsupported: tmux does not tell a pane's unsent input from what it printed | unsupported: Windows Terminal cannot read a pane's input | unsupported: Terminal cannot read a pane's input | unsupported: GNOME Terminal cannot read a pane's input | unsupported: Konsole cannot read a pane's input | unsupported: the terminal cannot read a pane's input |
